name: ConsoleSettings
vision: A generic admin console's own curated UI facts — nav, columns, state tones, which rows a detail panel shows — as real dispatched data instead of a hand-rewritten YAML file. A UI opinion the DOMAIN it's pointed at has no way to answer, never a business record; see the console app's own presentation_config.rb for the fuller story.

aggregates.name: StateStyle
aggregates.description: One aggregate's one lifecycle state, styled — a tone and whether it needs attention. Every real state gets a row, even a bare one (PresentationConfig's own missing_state_entries! check), so Declare and the two Set commands are separate: a bare row is a real, valid thing to have.

commands.name: Declare
commands.goal: Give one aggregate's one state a presentation row, styled or bare

givens.description: a style names its own aggregate
a style names its own state

commands.name: SetTone
commands.goal: Color one state

commands.name: SetAttention
commands.goal: Mark whether one state needs a person's attention

commands.name: SetExtra
commands.goal: Carry whatever per-state fields aren't individually modeled yet (label, note, ...)

aggregates.name: Collection
aggregates.description: One app aggregate's own console presentation — how it is named in the nav, where it sits, which field stands in for a whole record, and which query lists it. Its columns, detail-panel fields, identity assignment, preconditions and field formats are each a consistency boundary of their own: CollectionLayout, CollectionIdentity and CollectionRules, keyed by the same `agg`.

commands.name: Declare
commands.goal: Give one app aggregate a presentation row, before anything is curated on it yet

givens.description: a collection names its own aggregate

commands.goal: Name which field stands in for a whole record

commands.name: SetListQuery
commands.goal: Name which of an aggregate's own queries lists its records

commands.name: SetExtra
commands.goal: Carry whatever per-collection fields aren't individually modeled yet (noun_sing, create_label, nav_group, ...)

aggregates.name: CollectionIdentity
aggregates.description: How one app aggregate's console assigns its own new records' identity — the field, the strategy (slug, sequence or a port), and the strategy's source and prefix. One consistency boundary: a strategy and its prefix change together or not at all.

commands.name: Declare
commands.goal: Give one app aggregate's identity a row, before anything is curated on it yet

givens.description: a identity names its own aggregate

commands.name: SetIdentity
commands.goal: Name how a collection assigns its own new records' identity

aggregates.name: CollectionLayout
aggregates.description: What one app aggregate's console shows: the table columns, the detail-panel fields (with an optional entity state_filter and a row_columns subset). Every list-shaped piece is rows on this root, never a nested list inside a value object — no value object here can hold a map, and this sidesteps ever finding out whether one can hold a plain list either. Each list is replaced whole, never patched.

commands.name: Declare
commands.goal: Give one app aggregate's layout a row, before anything is curated on it yet

givens.description: a layout names its own aggregate

commands.goal: Replace a collection's own whole list of detail-panel fields

commands.goal: Replace every rows-field's own sub-column filter, whole

aggregates.name: CollectionRules
aggregates.description: The rules one app aggregate's console applies: the dispatch preconditions that gate a command on a field's state, and the display format of each field. Each list is replaced whole, never patched.

commands.name: Declare
commands.goal: Give one app aggregate's rules a row, before anything is curated on it yet

aggregates.name: Overview
aggregates.description: The console's own dashboard stat cards, whole. One row, ever — `key` is always the literal 'overview', never chosen. Every stat gets replaced as a whole list on save, the same 'replace whole, never patch one' convention CollectionLayout's and CollectionRules' own lists already use.
